//: Without this, Vercel deploys nothing but static files. Its zero-config step
sees a directory named public/, concludes the project is a static site,
publishes those three files and never looks for the server entrypoint — so
the UI loads and every /api and /v1 path is a 404. Deleting public/ is no
answer either: the whole project then gets published as static, src/ and all.
Declaring a build turns zero-config off. One function from server.mjs, one
catch-all route into it, no static output at all — which is right, because
this app serves its own files and gates them on the same token as the data.
